doc.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013

title: Collecting jazz magazines at the Grosvenor Library
summary: As a teenager he took notes on Jazz Reviews, Metronome and Esquire at the downtown library; a librarian friend found old Esquires for him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah, right. Is he a pitcher for the Philadelphia Phillies? I knew every baseball player so I was pretty good there, and you know, was a basketball kid. But I had this other passion. So on weekends I’d go to the Grosvener Library, the downtown library, and they would have these magazines down in the subbasement. And I would get them called up, and they’d get to know who I was so as soon as I walked in I’d go, “I want the Jazz Reviews” you know, “of all the ones I didn’t read last week.” And I’d take notes on them. And then the old Metronomes, and in those days Esquire wrote about jazz too.

Beautiful. One of the librarians, my girlfriend’s a librarian at Buffalo State, Butler Library, they were cleaning things out and she found a number of the old Esquires from 1942, ’43, ’44. She says, “This is for Chuck, oh my God.” So, you know, anything I could find I would just collect.
Plus they sponsored that photo that became “A Great Day in Harlem.”
